requirements.summary: Review and define acceptance criteria for the Work Item CRUD API endpoints, input validation, and error handling.
acceptance_criteria: POST /work-items creates a new item with a required title (max 100 chars) and optional description (max 1000 chars), returning HTTP 201 with the created item data.
GET /work-items retrieves all existing work items ordered by ID in descending order with HTTP 200.
PATCH /work-items/{item_id} allows updating the status field (max 50 chars) and returns HTTP 200 with the updated item.
PATCH /work-items/{item_id} returns HTTP 404 Not Found when attempting to update a non-existent item ID.
DELETE /work-items/{item_id} deletes the specified work item and returns HTTP 200 with deletion confirmation, or HTTP 404 if the item is not found.
Payload validation errors (e.g. missing title or exceeding max length) are rejected with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
Database and server-side errors are caught gracefully and return HTTP 500 Internal Server Error without leaking internal stack traces.

architecture.summary: The application lacks separation of concerns, mixes database access and schema definitions directly within API route handlers, and duplicates database connectivity logic.
findings: Separation of concerns: Database queries (raw SQL), Pydantic schemas, and route handling are all coupled in main.py instead of being structured into dedicated layers (e.g., schemas, repositories/services, routers).

Dual database connectivity: main.py instantiates an isolated ConnectionPool while also importing database_health from src.app.db, leading to fragmented database lifecycle and configuration management.

Unbounded query contract: The GET /work-items endpoint performs an unconstrained SELECT query without limit/offset or pagination controls, posing performance and memory exhaustion risks as the dataset grows.
Observability and error handling: Generic except Exception blocks suppress all underlying database/system errors without logging, hindering operational diagnosis.

qa_security.summary: The implementation introduces potential Denial of Service (DoS) risks via unbounded data queries, lacks strict domain validation on state transitions, and mixes blocking connection pool management inside async lifespan hooks.
security_risks: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion due to unbounded query execution without pagination limits.
Data integrity risk due to unvalidated status field strings in WorkItemUpdate allowing arbitrary state injection.
Synchronous blocking I/O (ConnectionPool.open/close) executed within async lifespan context, potentially starving the event loop.
Information suppression and blind exception catching without structured logging or auditing of database failures.

human_approval.note: Architektur- und QA-Findings (Separation of Concerns, Pagination, Enums) sind valide, überschreiten jedoch den Scope des Session 2 MVPs. Basis-Anforderungen (CRUD, grundlegendes Pooling, Error-Masking) sind vollständig erfüllt. Offene Punkte werden als Technical Debt ins Backlog übernommen. Freigabe als 'Accepted Risk' erteilt.
